results.text: AMEC WORKFLOW ProposalOps ⓘ Inputs & Go-Live 2 SYNTHETIC PROTOTYPE DEMO AS Owner Business Development Engineering SA OPERATING GUIDE A business guide to the current AMEC workflow ← Back to AMEC Work English العربي PROPOSAL · CONTRACT · PERMIT · AMEC ProposalOps helps AMEC move work from tender and proposal through contract and permit — with one controlled record of sources, decisions, handoffs, and next actions. Tender and client evidence, Proposal preparation, Engineering input, commercial review, Contract handoff, Permit preparation, Municipality status, comments, and corrections stay connected to the same governed work context. ✓ AI helps read, compare, extract, summarize, and prepare information. Deterministic workflow controls and authorized people remain responsible for consequential decisions. 01 SOURCE Tender · Client · Forms → 02 GOVERNED WORK Proposal · Contract · Permit → 03 CONTROLLED HANDOFF Right person · next action 01 SECTION 01 Why ProposalOps exists One opportunity, many sources Tender email, RFQ/RFP, client information, documents, photos, forms, Excel, and project evidence can all contribute to one controlled intake. Originals remain evidence; important values stay traceable. Keep current facts traceable ProposalOps keeps source identity, version, verification, and current-value context connected so teams can review what a value came from. Make handoffs and next actions visible BD → Engineering, Engineering → BD, Proposal → Contract, and Contract → Permit stay visible instead of disappearing between teams. 02 SECTION 02 The AMEC workflow This is one connected workflow from tender evidence through Municipality and Authority tracking. Permit is important downstream work, but it is not the whole ProposalOps product. 1 Tender / Client Sources Capture tender emails, documents, images, client information, and lists as evidence for the opportunity. 2 New Proposal Intake Start a source-driven Proposal with the commercial and contextual information AMEC has available. 3 Engineering Proposal Preparation Engineering prepares technical content, assumptions, exclusions, and the Proposal Form. 4 Business Development Review BD reviews the commercial position, coordinates the client response, and owns the next commercial action. 5 Contract A Contract is linked to the originating Proposal and the same Project context when the lifecycle reaches that point. 6 Contract Handoff The ready Contract opens the controlled downstream handoff into Permit work without losing the commercial context. 7 Permit → Municipality / Authority Permit teams prepare, verify, package, track authority status, resolve corrections, and keep the final submission human-controlled. The logical order remains 1 through 7 for screen readers. 03 SECTION 03 Who does what Owner See the cross-functional picture across Proposal, Contract, and Permit work: what is blocked, waiting, overdue, or moving between teams. Visibility does not override protected professional or consequential controls. Business Development Own tender/RFQ intake, client information, commercial Proposal fields, price, payment conditions, tracking, review, client response, Contract, and Contract → Permit handoff. Engineering Own Proposal Preparation: SOW, Process of Work, technical assumptions, technical exclusions, source review, Proposal Form, and technical comments back to BD. Engineering does not own binding price, payment terms, commercial release, or Contract execution. 04 SECTION 04 How Proposal work starts Tender / Client Sources Tender Email, Tender Document, Tender Photo / Image, Client Information, and Client List are source evidence. ProposalOps may capture candidate information where supported; important values remain traceable and are not assumed to be correct automatically. Provisional → canonical reference Early work can use a controlled Proposal / Opportunity Reference before AMEC assigns the final Project Reference. Once assigned, Proposal, Contract, Permit, and project evidence align to one Project context without losing history. New Proposal fields New Proposal may include Client, Proposal Description, Price, SOW, Period, Exclusions, Inclusions, Payment Condition, Process of Work, and other configured fields. The intake is source-driven; progressive fields may appear as context becomes available. Evidence stays evidence. ProposalOps can capture candidate information where supported, but it does not overclaim extraction accuracy or turn every file into an accepted fact automatically. 05 SECTION 05 Proposal Preparation and handoffs Proceed Proceed means Proposal Intake has enough verified information to move into Engineering Proposal Preparation. It does not mean save, commercial approval, Contract creation, or external submission. Engineering → BD Engineering prepares technical content and comments; BD receives the handoff for commercial review, client response, and the next lifecycle action. Business Development review BD reviews price, payment conditions, inclusions, exclusions, period, client context, and the commercial readiness of the Proposal. 06 SECTION 06 Proposal → Contract → Permit Proposals & Contracts is the commercial portfolio: it brings Proposal and Contract state together and opens the correct business context. 01 Sources Tender, client, and form evidence 02 Proposal register Description, Project Ref., stage, amount, last activity 03 Contract register Contract Ref., related Proposal, amount, end date Proposal → Contract A Contract is created or linked only at the correct lifecycle point. It stays linked to the originating Proposal and the same Project context; if one exists, users open it instead of accidentally creating a duplicate. Project Reference vs Contract Reference Project Reference identifies the AMEC project. Contract Reference identifies the Contract. They are separate business references even when shown together. Contract → Permit Permit work begins from the Contract when Contract and Project context are ready. The downstream Permit record preserves Proposal → Contract → Project → Permit relationships; one Contract is not promised to equal one Permit. 07 SECTION 07 Downstream Permit workflow These Permit stages remain accurate downstream work, but they follow the Proposal → Contract lifecycle rather than defining the whole product. 1 · Sources Confirm the correct Project, reference, and source connections. 2 · Verify Resolve key field conflicts and confirm trusted values. 3 · Package Prepare forms, documents, attachments, and package readiness. 4 · Municipality Prepare and validate the Municipality-side draft through the supported assisted or synthetic workflow. 5 · Final Review Confirm blockers are clear and prepare for the authorized human submission step. 6 · Authority Track Municipality / Authority status, comments, and returned changes. 7 · Corrections Resolve findings, create corrected revisions, and prepare the next controlled cycle. 8 · History Review revisions, events, evidence, and prior actions. Final submission stays human-controlled. ProposalOps prepares, validates, and tracks Municipality work, but the final external submission remains with an authorized human. 08 SECTION 08 AMEC Work, Issues, and Notifications AMEC Work What I need to DO: prioritized work across Proposal, Contract, Permit, handoffs, and exceptions. Open each item in its exact business context. Issues What is BLOCKING, WRONG, or AT RISK: missing sources, conflicts, commercial divergence, technical blockers, drawing mismatch, package blockers, or Authority Findings. Issues are not another task list. Notifications What CHANGED and what I should KNOW: handoffs, completed preparation, Contract creation, Permit initiation, Authority status, findings, or communication changes. Reading one does not complete the underlying work. Visible handoffs BD → Engineering · Engineering → BD · Proposal → Contract · Contract → Permit 09 SECTION 09 How information stays controlled 01 SOURCE Original evidence and version identity ↓ 02 GOVERNED WORK Proposal · Contract · Permit ↓ 03 CURRENT VALUE Reviewed value with traceability ↓ 04 CONTROLLED FORMS Proposal Form · Contract Form · Municipality forms ↓ 05 AUDIT / HISTORY Versions, events, and prior actions One shared truth Owner, Business Development, and Engineering see different views and actions, but they do not maintain shadow versions of the same Proposal, Contract, or Permit. Source provenance and read-back Original evidence stays connected to its project context and version. When a controlled source is registered, the stored result is read back and checked before it is treated as registered evidence. Forms derive from governed work Proposal Form, Contract Form, Municipality forms, Excel/status projections, and client communications derive from the same governed record wherever supported. Visual semantics Orange represents explicit human-controlled source input or lifecycle action, such as Tender Document, Proposal Form, Contract, Permit, or Proceed. Blue represents system-derived state, status, counts, and portfolio information. Verified/current styling means governed information, not unrestricted editing. 10 SECTION 10 Where AI helps — and where it does not AI AI may help with Reading documents Extracting candidate fields Comparing and summarizing sources Preparing drafts Identifying potential conflicts Supporting Authority precheck H People and controls decide Legal identity Professional compliance Binding price and terms Contract authority Consequential engineering decisions Final Municipality submission Deterministic workflow Workflow state, eligibility, blocking rules, references, permissions, and consequential transitions are controlled by deterministic application logic, not free-form AI judgment. 11 SECTION 11 Administration and Inputs & Go-Live Administration Owner-facing configuration and system status: People & Access, Data & Connections, Project & Folder Setup, Proposal / Contract Setup, Permit Setup, Templates, Notifications, Integration Health, Audit, and Advanced Diagnostics. Business Development and Engineering do not normally receive global Administration access. Inputs & Go-Live Administration explains how the product is configured. Inputs & Go-Live explains what AMEC still needs to provide or configure for real production operation: Needed, Requested, Provided, Configured, Tested, Ready, or Not Needed. Synthetic prototype truth The demonstration uses synthetic AMEC-style data and simulated external integrations. Internal workflow, relationships, controls, and persistence exercise real application behavior; live client/government credentials and production data are not used. 12 SECTION 12 Follow one job end to end 01 Tender source arrives 02 BD starts Proposal 03 Proposal information is captured and verified 04 BD selects Proceed 05 Engineering prepares technical content 06 Engineering hands back to BD 07 Proposal reaches Contract 08 Contract stays linked to Proposal and Project 09 Contract starts or opens downstream Permit 10 Engineering works through Permit stages 11 Authority changes are tracked 12 Corrections and history remain traceable 13 SECTION 13 Where do I start? Owner Start at AMEC Work, see what needs attention across teams, then open the Proposal, Contract, or Permit context. Business Development Start at AMEC Work or Proposals & Contracts for tender, Proposal, Contract, and commercial handoff work. Engineering Start at AMEC Work for Proposal Preparation or downstream technical Permit work. NEXT STEP Ready to work? Choose the surface that matches the next action in front of you. results.text: AMEC WORKFLOW ProposalOps ⓘ Inputs & Go-Live 2 SYNTHETIC PROTOTYPE DEMO AS Owner Business Development Engineering SA OPERATING GUIDE A business guide to the current AMEC workflow ← Back to AMEC Work English العربي PROPOSAL · CONTRACT · PERMIT · AMEC ProposalOps helps AMEC move work from tender and proposal through contract and permit — with one controlled record of sources, decisions, handoffs, and next actions. Tender and client evidence, Proposal preparation, Engineering input, commercial review, Contract handoff, Permit preparation, Municipality status, comments, and corrections stay connected to the same governed work context. ✓ AI helps read, compare, extract, summarize, and prepare information. Deterministic workflow controls and authorized people remain responsible for consequential decisions. 01 SOURCE Tender · Client · Forms → 02 GOVERNED WORK Proposal · Contract · Permit → 03 CONTROLLED HANDOFF Right person · next action 01 SECTION 01 Why ProposalOps exists One opportunity, many sources Tender email, RFQ/RFP, client information, documents, photos, forms, Excel, and project evidence can all contribute to one controlled intake. Originals remain evidence; important values stay traceable. Keep current facts traceable ProposalOps keeps source identity, version, verification, and current-value context connected so teams can review what a value came from. Make handoffs and next actions visible BD → Engineering, Engineering → BD, Proposal → Contract, and Contract → Permit stay visible instead of disappearing between teams. 02 SECTION 02 The AMEC workflow This is one connected workflow from tender evidence through Municipality and Authority tracking. Permit is important downstream work, but it is not the whole ProposalOps product. 1 Tender / Client Sources Capture tender emails, documents, images, client information, and lists as evidence for the opportunity. 2 New Proposal Intake Start a source-driven Proposal with the commercial and contextual information AMEC has available. 3 Engineering Proposal Preparation Engineering prepares technical content, assumptions, exclusions, and the Proposal Form. 4 Business Development Review BD reviews the commercial position, coordinates the client response, and owns the next commercial action. 5 Contract A Contract is linked to the originating Proposal and the same Project context when the lifecycle reaches that point. 6 Contract Handoff The ready Contract opens the controlled downstream handoff into Permit work without losing the commercial context. 7 Permit → Municipality / Authority Permit teams prepare, verify, package, track authority status, resolve corrections, and keep the final submission human-controlled. The logical order remains 1 through 7 for screen readers. 03 SECTION 03 Who does what Owner See the cross-functional picture across Proposal, Contract, and Permit work: what is blocked, waiting, overdue, or moving between teams. Visibility does not override protected professional or consequential controls. Business Development Own tender/RFQ intake, client information, commercial Proposal fields, price, payment conditions, tracking, review, client response, Contract, and Contract → Permit handoff. Engineering Own Proposal Preparation: SOW, Process of Work, technical assumptions, technical exclusions, source review, Proposal Form, and technical comments back to BD. Engineering does not own binding price, payment terms, commercial release, or Contract execution. 04 SECTION 04 How Proposal work starts Tender / Client Sources Tender Email, Tender Document, Tender Photo / Image, Client Information, and Client List are source evidence. ProposalOps may capture candidate information where supported; important values remain traceable and are not assumed to be correct automatically. Provisional → canonical reference Early work can use a controlled Proposal / Opportunity Reference before AMEC assigns the final Project Reference. Once assigned, Proposal, Contract, Permit, and project evidence align to one Project context without losing history. New Proposal fields New Proposal may include Client, Proposal Description, Price, SOW, Period, Exclusions, Inclusions, Payment Condition, Process of Work, and other configured fields. The intake is source-driven; progressive fields may appear as context becomes available. Evidence stays evidence. ProposalOps can capture candidate information where supported, but it does not overclaim extraction accuracy or turn every file into an accepted fact automatically. 05 SECTION 05 Proposal Preparation and handoffs Proceed Proceed means Proposal Intake has enough verified information to move into Engineering Proposal Preparation. It does not mean save, commercial approval, Contract creation, or external submission. Engineering → BD Engineering prepares technical content and comments; BD receives the handoff for commercial review, client response, and the next lifecycle action. Business Development review BD reviews price, payment conditions, inclusions, exclusions, period, client context, and the commercial readiness of the Proposal. 06 SECTION 06 Proposal → Contract → Permit Proposals & Contracts is the commercial portfolio: it brings Proposal and Contract state together and opens the correct business context. 01 Sources Tender, client, and form evidence 02 Proposal register Description, Project Ref., stage, amount, last activity 03 Contract register Contract Ref., related Proposal, amount, end date Proposal → Contract A Contract is created or linked only at the correct lifecycle point. It stays linked to the originating Proposal and the same Project context; if one exists, users open it instead of accidentally creating a duplicate. Project Reference vs Contract Reference Project Reference identifies the AMEC project. Contract Reference identifies the Contract. They are separate business references even when shown together. Contract → Permit Permit work begins from the Contract when Contract and Project context are ready. The downstream Permit record preserves Proposal → Contract → Project → Permit relationships; one Contract is not promised to equal one Permit. 07 SECTION 07 Downstream Permit workflow These Permit stages remain accurate downstream work, but they follow the Proposal → Contract lifecycle rather than defining the whole product. 1 · Sources Confirm the correct Project, reference, and source connections. 2 · Verify Resolve key field conflicts and confirm trusted values. 3 · Package Prepare forms, documents, attachments, and package readiness. 4 · Municipality Prepare and validate the Municipality-side draft through the supported assisted or synthetic workflow. 5 · Final Review Confirm blockers are clear and prepare for the authorized human submission step. 6 · Authority Track Municipality / Authority status, comments, and returned changes. 7 · Corrections Resolve findings, create corrected revisions, and prepare the next controlled cycle. 8 · History Review revisions, events, evidence, and prior actions. Final submission stays human-controlled. ProposalOps prepares, validates, and tracks Municipality work, but the final external submission remains with an authorized human. 08 SECTION 08 AMEC Work, Issues, and Notifications AMEC Work What I need to DO: prioritized work across Proposal, Contract, Permit, handoffs, and exceptions. Open each item in its exact business context. Issues What is BLOCKING, WRONG, or AT RISK: missing sources, conflicts, commercial divergence, technical blockers, drawing mismatch, package blockers, or Authority Findings. Issues are not another task list. Notifications What CHANGED and what I should KNOW: handoffs, completed preparation, Contract creation, Permit initiation, Authority status, findings, or communication changes. Reading one does not complete the underlying work. Visible handoffs BD → Engineering · Engineering → BD · Proposal → Contract · Contract → Permit 09 SECTION 09 How information stays controlled 01 SOURCE Original evidence and version identity ↓ 02 GOVERNED WORK Proposal · Contract · Permit ↓ 03 CURRENT VALUE Reviewed value with traceability ↓ 04 CONTROLLED FORMS Proposal Form · Contract Form · Municipality forms ↓ 05 AUDIT / HISTORY Versions, events, and prior actions One shared truth Owner, Business Development, and Engineering see different views and actions, but they do not maintain shadow versions of the same Proposal, Contract, or Permit. Source provenance and read-back Original evidence stays connected to its project context and version. When a controlled source is registered, the stored result is read back and checked before it is treated as registered evidence. Forms derive from governed work Proposal Form, Contract Form, Municipality forms, Excel/status projections, and client communications derive from the same governed record wherever supported. Visual semantics Orange represents explicit human-controlled source input or lifecycle action, such as Tender Document, Proposal Form, Contract, Permit, or Proceed. Blue represents system-derived state, status, counts, and portfolio information. Verified/current styling means governed information, not unrestricted editing. 10 SECTION 10 Where AI helps — and where it does not AI AI may help with Reading documents Extracting candidate fields Comparing and summarizing sources Preparing drafts Identifying potential conflicts Supporting Authority precheck H People and controls decide Legal identity Professional compliance Binding price and terms Contract authority Consequential engineering decisions Final Municipality submission Deterministic workflow Workflow state, eligibility, blocking rules, references, permissions, and consequential transitions are controlled by deterministic application logic, not free-form AI judgment. 11 SECTION 11 Administration and Inputs & Go-Live Administration Owner-facing configuration and system status: People & Access, Data & Connections, Project & Folder Setup, Proposal / Contract Setup, Permit Setup, Templates, Notifications, Integration Health, Audit, and Advanced Diagnostics. Business Development and Engineering do not normally receive global Administration access. Inputs & Go-Live Administration explains how the product is configured.
